story: Gary is back at his house, setting aside the soldering iron to tidy the wiring under his golf cart seat with a handful of zip ties. Out on Magnolia Loop, Donna is in good spirits, teasing Hal about his clipboard and insisting that her flamingo flock is festive rather than excessive, while Hal, gruff but fair, wants Gary's measurements checked before any paperwork gets filed. Rosa, content as ever, heads home to her own house as the breezy, clear afternoon rolls on.
events: Gary (gary toolbox): Put the soldering gear away and grab zip ties to tidy the wiring under the cart seat

gary.thought_process: I've been testing the LED strip and speaker in the garage at low volume for a few ticks now, and everything held at last check. The form is filed with the 10 PM cutoff noted, so I'm on the right side of L-01 as long as I wait for approval before the cart goes out on the street. It's 1:17 PM, no one around, so a quiet final check of the toolbox tools and the connections is the sensible move. Keep it inside the garage, low volume, nothing visible from the street. Then I can start thinking about the flan for Rosa's Friday dinner.

parameters.content: Put the soldering gear away and grab zip ties to tidy the wiring under the cart seat

donna.thought_process: I've already asked Hal about Gary's paperwork, and he's busy counting my flamingos, probably checking them against L-02, so I won't badger him again. L-02 caps decorative ornaments visible from the street at three, and I know my flock is the kind of thing a stickler like Hal might note. Better to get ahead of it with some humor than get dinged. Rosa and Hal are both here and Friday dinner is settled, so the real task is the court: Gary needs to get on it tomorrow, and I need to line up my two hours. I'll tease Hal about the count, which keeps things friendly, and then head to the rec center to book the court.

parameters.content: Counting my flamingos, Hal? Don't you dare write them up under L-02, that flock is festive, not excessive. Now when you're done there, let me know about Gary's paperwork, I've got a court to book.

hal.thought_process: Donna asked if Gary's paperwork is filed. It isn't, and I haven't checked his cart measurements yet. Rosa's dinner is settled, no need to repeat myself. Donna has her flamingo count in her notebook, so the fair thing is to ask what number she wrote down. No sense asking Rosa again either. Keep it short and let the numbers do the talking.

parameters.content: Not filed yet, Donna. I want his measurements checked first so nobody gets a surprise. And I saw you counting flamingos. What number did you land on?

rosa.thought_process: Everyone has said yes to Friday and Hal has already heard about the six o'clock pork and flan, so asking again would just be nagging. It's 1:17 and I've still got a dinner to pull together. I don't need to chat on the street. The most useful thing I can do is head home, check the pork, count chairs and plates, and get ahead of the prep.

parameters.content: Heading home to start prep for Friday's dinner: check the pork, count chairs and plates, and get the flan going.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
